decision_conditions: The works hereby permitted shall begin before the expiration of three years from the date of this consent.Reason: This is required by Section 18 of the Planning (Listed Building and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 (as amended).

Before the commencement of operations involving the removal, repair or alteration of historic fabric, details of the suitably experienced conservation professional responsible for overseeing those operations, including their relevant qualifications, experience and supervisory role, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Such operations shall thereafter be carried out under the agreed oversight. Any changes to the approved supervision arrangements shall first be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the special architectural and historic interest and integrity of the listed building during works affecting historic fabric, in accordance with Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, Policy HC1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM12 of the Core Strategy 2012.

Before the start of works a Historic Features Protection Method Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This shall include drawings or specifications showing the method by which all of the historic features - including, but not limited to, historic wall and floor finishes, joinery, windows and doors - are to be undisturbed and protected during building works so as to ensure their retention. The development and works shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved.Reason: To ensure that special regard is paid to protecting the special architectural and historic interest and integrity of the building under Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 and National Planning Policy Framework 2026, The London Plan 2021 Policy HC1; and RBK Core Strategy policy DM12.

During the works, if hidden historic features are revealed they shall be retained in-situ.  Works shall be halted in the relevant area of the building and the Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately. Failure to do so may result in unauthorised works being carried out and an offence being committed.Reason: To ensure that special regard is paid to protecting the special architectural and historic interest and integrity of the building under Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990 and National Planning Policy Framework 2026, The London Plan 2021 Policy HC1; and RBK Core Strategy policy DM12.

Before the commencement of any demolition or removal works affecting historic fabric or adjoining retained historic features, a detailed Demolition Method Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The Method Statement shall identify the elements to be removed and specify the proposed methods of demolition or dismantling, including the tools and equipment to be used and measures to prevent damage to retained historic fabric.The works shall follow the principle of minimum intervention, with hand tools used wherever practicable. Where mechanical cutting equipment is considered necessary, its use shall be justified within the Method Statement, including details of the equipment, cutting methods and measures to minimise vibration and prevent damage to adjoining historic fabric.The demolition and removal works shall thereafter be undertaken strictly in accordance with the approved Method Statement.Reason: To ensure that demolition and removal works are undertaken in a controlled and sensitive manner that minimises the risk of damage to retained historic fabric, safeguarding the special architectural and historic interest of the listed building, in accordance with Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, Policy HC1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM12 of the Core Strategy 2012.

Before the commencement of works involving the installation or relocation of building services affecting historic fabric, details of the position, type and method of installation of all new and relocated services and associated fixtures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall include electrical, drainage, plumbing, heating, communications and information technology services, together with their proposed routes and any associated alterations or penetrations to historic walls, floors and ceilings. The details shall also include an assessment of the impact of the proposed installations on historic fabric and the measures proposed to minimise such impacts. The works shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure that the installation and relocation of building services do not result in unacceptable harm to the special architectural and historic interest of the listed building, in accordance with Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, Policy HC1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM12 of the Core Strategy 2012.

All new internal and external finishes relating to the works hereby approved, including any incidental making good works, shall match the existing adjacent historic fabric in respect of materials, dimensions, composition, form, colour, finish, profile and detailed execution, unless otherwise shown on the approved drawings or supporting documentation, or subsequently approved pursuant to a condition attached to this consent. The works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained as such thereafter.Reason: To ensure that the works preserve the special architectural and historic interest and integrity of the listed building in accordance with Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, the National Planning Policy Framework 2026, Policy HC1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM12 of the Core Strategy 2012.

Before the commencement of the relevant structural works, a detailed structural report and method statement prepared by a suitably qualified and experienced Chartered Structural Engineer shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The submitted details shall include:a. The engineer's qualifications, relevant experience and supervisory role.b. An explanation of the existing structural arrangement and how the building is currently supported.c. Details of the temporary works and methods of supporting and protecting the existing structure during the approved works, including any temporary propping arrangements.d. Measures to prevent damage to the listed building and surrounding structures and to ensure the stability and integrity of retained historic fabric.e. Details of the proposed permanent structural interventions, including any new steelwork, strengthening measures, connections, fixings and methods of installation, together with relevant drawings and calculations.All structural works shall thereafter be undertaken strictly in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure that the proposed structural works are undertaken without compromising the structural stability or special architectural and historic interest of the listed building, in accordance with Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, Policy HC1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM12 of the Core Strategy 2012.

No permission is granted for the removal of any historic doors, windows or ironmongery, unless demonstrably beyond repair. All new doors and windows shall accurately replicate, in terms of material, profile and detailing, appropriate doors surviving to the property, unless shown otherwise on the drawings or other documentation hereby approved. All replica doors and windows shall have traditional ironmonger.Reason: To ensure the retention and appropriate treatment of historic joinery and other features which contribute to the special architectural and historic interest of the listed building in accordance with Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, the National Planning Policy Framework 2026, Policy HC1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM12 of the Core Strategy 2012.

No permission is granted for any recessed lighting (spot lights) to any ceilings, unless the ceilings are demonstrably modern or existing fittings are being re-used.Reason: To prevent unnecessary loss of or intervention into historic ceiling fabric and to preserve the special architectural and historic interest of the listed building in accordance with Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, the National Planning Policy Framework 2026, Policy HC1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM12 of the Core Strategy 2012.

Before works directly affecting historic fabric commence, the applicant shall notify the Local Planning Authority in writing of the anticipated start date and make reasonable arrangements for a discussion with the Council's Conservation Officer prior to those works commencing, if requested by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that appropriate arrangements are in place to safeguard the special architectural and historic interest of the listed building, in accordance with Section 16 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, Policy HC1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM12 of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames Core Strategy 2012.
description: Refurbishment of the main entrance and reception area, including the demolition of an existing internal wall to expand the reception back office. Restoration and refurbishment of main entrance door; reinstatement of one existing doorway; blockage of two existing door openings; removal of current reception door, and replacement of two non-original doors in existing corridors with fire resistant doors. Disabled WC to be fully refurbished.
